Lessons.Title: Find Factors and Multiples
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 first-edition IM Grade4 Unit1 Lesson7: use factor and multiple terms for whole numbers1–100. The four-page Student Task Statements PDF and teacher lesson are the original sources; existing correct Edulytics goals/introduction are retained.
Warm-up 10 minutes Number Talk: 12÷3=4, 30÷3=10, 60÷3=20, 72÷3=24; teacher discusses relation 12+60=72 and distributive division.

Activity1 15 minutes: for each original source number10,7,50,16,35,20,19,6 complete TWO open statements, one '___ is a factor of ___ because...' and one '___ is a multiple of ___ because...'. A mathematically correct statement must have a valid whole-number multiplication/division reason. Partner shares one notice and one wonder. Teacher evaluates open language and all eight rows.

Activity2 20 minutes: Find the Number Stage2, DIFFERENT from earlier Stage1. Use the 1–100 printed gameboard. Starter picks an even integer less than50; partner selects an UNCOVERED factor or multiple of the previous selected number. Alternate until no valid uncovered factor/multiple remains. Last player to cover a number gets one point; play up to10 rounds and rotate starter. This is a physical, stateful teacher-led partner game; neither generic factors Practice nor Stage1 scoring substitutes for it.
Lesson synthesis 10 minutes: 1 is a factor of every number; 2 of each even number; multiples of5 end0 or5; multiples of10 end0. Revisit exact meaning of factors and multiples.

Independent Edulytics five-minute Cool-down (user-authorised, NOT the restricted publisher-original): write one true factor statement and one true multiple statement about35 and justify them by multiplication. Example:5 factor of35 and35 multiple of5 because5×7=35. Teacher checks free reasoning; auto Practice grades a separate numeric decision.

KeyConcepts.Title: Factor
KeyConcepts.Definition: A positive whole number that divides a target exactly.
KeyConcepts.Rule: a is factor of b iff b%a=0.

KeyConcepts.Title: Multiple
KeyConcepts.Definition: A whole-number product of a positive number and a whole-number count.
KeyConcepts.Rule: b is a multiple of a iff b=a×k.

KeyConcepts.Title: Game move
KeyConcepts.Definition: Uncovered factor or multiple of last chosen number.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Start even <50, then always choose uncovered legal neighbor; one point for last successful move.
KeyConcepts.Example: If current is12, uncovered 3 or24 might be legal when on board1–100.

WorkedExamples.Title: 35 and7
WorkedExamples.Question: Complete a factor and a multiple statement.
Steps: State 7 is a factor of35 and35 is a multiple of7.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 35 is multiple of7, but7 is not multiple of35.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using Stage1 rules for source Stage2 game.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Stage2 has grid1–100 and one point for the final legal move.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep actual gameboard and covered state under teacher observation.

SummaryPoints: Exact source number list10,7,50,16,35,20,19,6 and TWO open sentence stems each.
Original Number Talk four divisions and partner observations retained.
Source Stage2 factors/multiples game start even<50, legal uncovered moves, one point to last player, up to10 rounds.
All student explanations and physical game actions are teacher-evaluated, distinct from numeric Practice.
Independent Edulytics five-minute Cool-down is goal-equivalent but not source-identical.
